hook.line: Vale wants Hernando to rest, and she says so two different ways in the same morning. Both are right, and a Colombian ear hears no difference. You just need to be able to build either one.

examples.en: I advise you to wait a little. (to a friend)

examples.en: I advise you to wait a little. (to a friend)
I advise you all to wait here.

examples.en: The doctor recommends that Hernando take the pill.

rule:
After *recomendar*, *aconsejar*, *permitir* and *prohibir* you have two choices.

1. The infinitive: *Le recomiendo descansar*. Shorter. The little word (*le*) says who rests.
2. *que* + a changed verb: *Le recomiendo que descanse*. Same meaning. The verb changes ending, like the *que* sentences you know from *quiero que*.

Use the infinitive when the person is just the little word. Use *que* when you name the person, or when it is easier to build the whole clause: *Le recomiendo a Hernando que descanse*.

One trap: *Quiero descansar* means I rest. *Quiero que descanses* means you rest.
smallPrint: Teachers call the first the infinitive construction and the second the subjunctive construction; both are correct after verbs of influence.

I recommend that you rested.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence: *Le recomiendo ___.* (*descansar* or *que descanse*) I recommend that you rest. (formal)
yourTurn.why: Both work: the infinitive alone, or *que* with the changed verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence: *Quiero que ___.* (*descansar* or *descanses*) I want you to rest. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: After *que* the verb changes ending, so *descanses*, not the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it the longer way with *que*: *Te aconsejo esperar un poco.*
yourTurn.answer: Te aconsejo que esperes un poco.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it the shorter way with an infinitive: *Te recomiendo que comas menos sal.*
Type in Spanish: I advise you all to wait here.
yourTurn.why: *Les* is "you all", and either way of building it works.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The doctor recommends that Hernando take the pill.
yourTurn.answer: La doctora le recomienda a Hernando que tome la pastilla.
accept: La doctora le recomienda tomar la pastilla a Hernando.
La doctora le recomienda a Hernando tomar la pastilla.
yourTurn.why: When you name the person, *que* is the easy way to build it.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I want to rest.
yourTurn.why: When you are the one who rests, there is no *que*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. After *que* the verb changes ending; it does not stay as the infinitive.
With *que*, the verb has to show who rests: *descanses* for "you".
If you are the one resting, just use the infinitive: *quiero descansar*.

personal: Tell us one thing you advise a friend to do, building it with *te aconsejo* once with an infinitive and once with *que*.
